data.command: How do I generate a packet capture for the last 5 minutes on interface eth0?

data.text:
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ sudo /usr/bin/tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/eth0_5min.pcap -G 300 -W 1
tcpdump: listening on eth0, link-type EN10MB (Ethernet), snapshot length 262144 bytes

^C
1834 packets captured
1841 packets received by filter
0 packets dropped by kernel
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ ls -lh /tmp/eth0_5min.pcap
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 1.7M Feb 14 11:47 /tmp/eth0_5min.pcap
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ tcpdump -r /tmp/eth0_5min.pcap -nn -c 5
reading from file /tmp/eth0_5min.pcap, link-type EN10MB (Ethernet)
11:42:03.114522 IP 10.0.0.12.443 > 10.0.0.51.51844: Flags [P.], seq 1:142, ack 1, win 501, length 141
11:42:03.114887 IP 10.0.0.51.51844 > 10.0.0.12.443: Flags [.], ack 142, win 502, length 0
11:42:03.241160 IP 10.0.0.12.22 > 10.0.0.7.49912: Flags [P.], seq 1:84, ack 1, win 509, length 83
11:42:04.009331 IP 10.0.0.12.443 > 10.0.0.51.51844: Flags [P.], seq 142:305, ack 1, win 501, length 163
11:42:04.009664 IP 10.0.0.51.51844 > 10.0.0.12.443: Flags [.], ack 305, win 501, length 0
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ 

Note: tcpdump only captures from the moment it starts — for a rolling buffer you'd need it already running (e.g. -G 300 -W 12 into a ring), there's no on-box history to pull the previous 5 minutes from.
